skill.name: kling-3-0
skill.description: Kling 3.0 RunComfy skill for generating text-to-video and image-to-video clips across Standard, Pro, and 4K tiers. It guides tier selection, prompt structure, CLI invocation, optional audio, image references, and output handling for RunComfy jobs.
skill.summary: Generate Kling 3.0 videos through RunComfy with tier selection, prompt guidance, and CLI command patterns.
skill.author: doany-ai

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, documentation links, and placeholder URLs. The real risks are persistent RunComfy token storage, authenticated third-party API execution, public image URL sharing, and local output directory writes.

remediation.suggestion: Document the token path and permissions clearly, require confirmation before runcomfy login, prefer scoped tokens, and include token removal steps.

remediation.issue: Authenticated external API calls and account billing
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before every RunComfy generation and show tier, duration, audio setting, output directory, and estimated cost.

remediation.issue: Public image URL submission to a third-party service
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to submit confidential images, internal URLs, or regulated data, and explain that RunComfy servers fetch image references.

remediation.issue: Generated media written to arbitrary output paths
remediation.suggestion: Use a safe default output directory, require approval for absolute paths, and warn before large 4K downloads.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples create noisy static command alerts
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as documentation and separate autonomous agent actions from commands a user must approve.

semantic_findings.title: Authenticated Third-Party Video API Calls
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs users or agents to install and run the RunComfy CLI, log in or provide RUNCOMFY_TOKEN, submit requests to the RunComfy Model API, poll status, and download generated outputs. This can send prompts and image references to a third party and can incur account charges without explicit approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 69-72 require the CLI and token, and lines 273-277 describe authenticated API submission and downloads. The behavior is explicitly documented.

semantic_findings.title: User-Provided Image URLs Leave Local Control
semantic_findings.description: The image-to-video workflow requires public HTTPS image URLs, and the document says RunComfy servers fetch those images. Users could expose private media or metadata to the service when animating reference images.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The requirements and privacy note state that image-to-video needs a public URL and that RunComfy servers fetch it. This directly supports the privacy finding.

semantic_findings.title: Downloaded Media Can Be Written to Arbitrary Output Directories
semantic_findings.description: The examples use an absolute output directory, and the workflow downloads generated media into that directory. An autonomous agent should not choose sensitive or unexpected local paths for large generated files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples and workflow explicitly reference an absolute output directory and downloaded result files. The file size cap lowers but does not remove local write risk.

content.value_statement: Creating Kling 3.0 clips requires choosing a tier, mode, duration, audio option, and prompt structure. This skill guides RunComfy CLI use for text-to-video and image-to-video jobs.
actual_capabilities: Explains all six Kling 3.0 RunComfy endpoints by tier and mode.
Recommends Standard, Pro, or 4K based on quality and cost needs.
Shows RunComfy CLI invocation patterns for text-to-video and image-to-video jobs.
Documents duration, aspect ratio, audio, seed, and prompt guidance fields.
Provides prompt patterns for multi-shot videos, portrait animation, and vertical shorts.
Summarizes limitations, pricing notes, exit codes, token storage, and outbound endpoints.
limitations: Requires RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and a valid login or token.
Image-to-video jobs require a public HTTPS image URL; local files are not supported.
Each generation is capped at 15 seconds, and supported aspect ratios are fixed.
The skill documents CLI usage but does not provide automated cost controls or content review.

use_cases.title: Create Social Video Drafts
use_cases.description: Generate short 1080p or vertical videos from written prompts for rapid campaign review.

use_cases.title: Plan High-Fidelity Brand Clips
use_cases.description: Compare Standard, Pro, and 4K tiers before committing budget to final video output.

use_cases.title: Prepare Repeatable Video Jobs
use_cases.description: Build consistent RunComfy CLI workflows for Kling 3.0 text-to-video and image-to-video tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Text Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to generate a 5 second Kling 3.0 Standard text-to-video clip for: [scene]. Use 16:9 and no audio.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Reference Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Kling 3.0 image-to-video with this public image URL: [url]. Preserve the subject and add: [motion].

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Pro Multi-Shot Ad
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Kling V3.0 Pro prompt with three shots for [product]. Include camera movement, stable identity, and optional audio.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a 4K Production Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose the best Kling 3.0 4K endpoint for [campaign]. Include duration, aspect ratio, audio choice, cost considerations, and RunComfy command guidance.

output_examples.input: A user wants a quick vertical cafe video for social media.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: Standard text-to-video, 5 seconds, vertical aspect ratio, and no audio for the first draft. The prompt should lead with close-up handheld motion and steam detail.

output_examples.input: A team has a product photo and wants hero footage.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: Pro image-to-video or 4K image-to-video, based on final resolution. Use an identity-preserving prompt and confirm the public image URL before submission.

output_examples.input: A director needs a multi-shot brand clip with voiceover.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: Pro text-to-video with audio for 1080p review. Move to 4K only after the script and shots are approved.

best_practices: Start with Standard for drafts, then move to Pro or 4K after the prompt is stable.
Confirm duration, audio, tier, and estimated cost before running RunComfy commands.
Use public image URLs only when you have permission to send them to RunComfy.
anti_patterns: Do not submit confidential images, internal URLs, or regulated content as image references.
Do not start with 4K for prompt exploration when Standard can validate the idea.
Do not request unsupported aspect ratios or clips longer than 15 seconds in one job.

faq.question: Does this skill run Kling 3.0 locally?
faq.answer: No. It guides the RunComfy CLI, which submits jobs to RunComfy services.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Do I need a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow requires RunComfy CLI login or RUNCOMFY_TOKEN.

faq.question: Can it animate a local file?
faq.answer: No. Image-to-video requires a public HTTPS image URL.

faq.question: What tier should I use first?
faq.answer: Use Standard for drafts, Pro for high-quality 1080p, and 4K for final native 4K output.

faq.question: What security review is needed before use?
faq.answer: Confirm token handling, cost, output directory, and third-party image sharing before running commands.
